name: How to Use PF2e Tavern Games

text.content:
How to Use PF2e Tavern Games

Open the game library

Enable PF2e Tavern Games, then use the dice button in Token controls, the PF2e Tavern Games button on an eligible character or NPC sheet, or the Open PF2e Tavern Games macro in the compendium. The GM chooses Poppy’s Prize from the existing table or opens the Tavern Games library to start Golem, Bounder, Century, or a Drinking Contest.

Participants and player panels

The GM selects eligible PC and NPC actors. For the card games, each player should have Owner permission on their actor. A player then opens their panel from their actor sheet or Token controls; the GM may use Open player panel on a table participant to prompt it remotely. The player panel contains only that actor’s private cards and legal controls. The GM retains final authority and may disqualify a participant from any game.

Game preparation

Golem requires three to six participants, Poppy’s Prize requires two to four, and Bounder, Century, and Drinking Contest accept two or more. For Golem, Bounder, Century, and Drinking Contest, the GM first selects the number of participants. The next dialogue provides one character selector for each participant. Each selector is ordered with - Dummy first, then Party Members, then other eligible actors alphabetically; after a count is chosen, each selector must identify a different real actor. The GM enters stakes using pp, gp, sp, and cp fields where relevant, then selects a Dealer or Shooter. Start buttons prepare a game; the designated Dealer or Shooter performs the first game action from their private panel or the GM table.

Golem card art

Golem renders its dealt cards with the supplied 53-image material deck: 52 numbered cards across Flesh, Clay, Stone, and Iron, plus golem_card_back.png. That supplied card-back PNG is used for concealed Golem cards, including marked-card sight. Only the 52 material-suit face cards enter the Golem deck.

Cheating

Any Poppy or Golem Dealer may cheat by choosing every card needed to complete their hand. They then select a blind Performance check or blind Deception check using Create a Diversion. Its result is compared with each other participant’s Perception DC; the GM and an observer receive a private suspicion whisper only if that comparison is a failure or critical failure. The module checks item slugs and never offers an equipment-based benefit without the matching item in the active role-holder’s inventory. Only the Poppy’s Prize or Golem deck owner with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Q4KkKGGXq4bNGHh2]{Marked Playing Cards} may use marked-card sight or choose the two special first-hand marked cards. Only a Bounder Shooter with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Q4KkKGGXq4bNGHh2]{Loaded Dice} may choose either d20 result; in Century, only the Dealer with Loaded Dice may choose the twenty results. A cheating drinking contestant uses the same blind Performance or Deception concealment choice but receives an automatic Fortitude success rather than choosing cards.

Dealer social cheating

When Poppy’s Prize or Golem is in the prepared Deal phase, the active Poppy or Dealer may check Cheat and choose my hand. The Dealer selects every card needed to complete their hand, then chooses either Performance or Deception — Create a Diversion. The GM validates the selection, resolves the concealment roll as blind, and compares it separately with every qualified observer’s Perception DC. A detected attempt sends a private suspicion message only to the observing actor’s active Owners and the GM; an undetected attempt sends no message. This social cheating route is available to every active Dealer. It does not reveal other hands. Marked Playing Cards remain required for the additional marked-card sight and special two-card opening selection.

Drinking Contest effects

The contest assigns and updates temporary PF2E conditions and a module-owned timed effect for each stage. Starting another drinking game or closing the contest clears effects created by the module; conditions that existed before the game are restored to their original values. Stage 6 sets unconscious for eight hours and removes the actor from the contest.

Results and reset

Every game maintains a shared activity log. Use Close table to clear the current multi-game state. Closing a drinking contest also clears its module-owned contest effects. Resetting does not reverse any currency changes that a GM has performed manually or through the original Poppy’s Prize automatic-currency option.

Source acknowledgement. Poppy’s Prize originates in Jewel of the Indigo Isles. Golem, Bounder, and Century originate in Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing, p. 76, as presented by Archives of Nethys. The drinking contest is a table rule supplied for this module.
